rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the 10 compounds and identify crowded retention regions while promoting complete elution. The results will guide adjustments to gradient range, duration, and temperature.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing how much of the current resolution margin remains. Keep temperature and solvent endpoints fixed to isolate the effect of gradient steepness.

Test temperature-driven selectivity changes to separate the crowded middle peaks without lengthening the gradient. The 10-minute gradient already eliminates the time penalty, so improving its two under-resolved pairs could reach the maximum score.

Slightly flatten the gradient to improve the remaining under-resolved pair while keeping the final peak near the zero-time-penalty region. This also tests whether the temperature-improved middle-peak separation survives the change in gradient slope.

Slightly flatten the gradient by lowering the final organic fraction, aiming to increase the narrow resolution margins while retaining a zero time penalty. This explores a nearby alternative to the method already achieving the maximum CRF.

Test the temperature sensitivity of the maximum-scoring method with a 5 °C increase. This may improve the marginal middle-pair separation, although another pair could become limiting; injection 4 remains the established optimum.

Test a slightly stronger starting solvent at the successful 55 °C temperature to explore a faster alternative with improved resolution margins. The maximum score is already secured; this injection probes whether it can be retained with a different gradient range.

Lower the final organic fraction to recover resolution in the limiting pair from injection 7. The slightly shallower gradient may retain the zero time penalty while bringing all adjacent pairs above 1.5.

Flatten the gradient one further step to lift the limiting resolution above 1.5 while preserving the other middle-pair separation. Extrapolation from injections 7–8 places the last peak near 8 minutes, potentially retaining the maximum CRF without a time penalty.

Combine a stronger starting solvent with a shallower gradient to seek another maximum-scoring method with improved resolution margins. These changes may offset one another in last-peak retention, keeping it near the zero-penalty boundary.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity with the short gradient to look for a separate maximum-scoring region. Cooling may separate the crowded middle peaks differently while keeping the last peak near the zero-time-penalty window; the established CRF 1.000 methods remain available.

Test 5 °C below the successful method to characterize its lower-temperature selectivity boundary. This should improve separation of the pair that deteriorated at 60 °C, while checking whether another middle pair becomes limiting.

Explore a stronger-starting, high-temperature gradient that may move the limiting middle pair past its selectivity crossover and restore separation in reversed order. This could yield a faster maximum-scoring alternative, but early-peak compression must also be checked.

Lower the starting organic fraction to improve the early-pair separation seen in injection 13, while shortening the gradient to explore separation beyond the middle-pair crossover. This tests a faster alternative without risking the already-established maximum score.

Steepen the gradient at the same starting composition and temperature to test whether the remaining close pair separates further beyond its crossover. Monitor the neighboring pair for compression while seeking a shorter maximum-scoring method.

Preserve injection 4’s successful gradient slope and temperature while ending the ramp earlier at a lower organic fraction. Since all peaks previously eluted by 7.60 minutes, before these gradients diverge, this method should retain the maximum CRF.

Keep the successful gradient slope and temperature while lowering the endpoint further. The outlet gradient remains identical through the observed last peak at 7.60 minutes, so this should preserve CRF 1.000 with a lower final organic fraction.

Use a gradient slope between injections 8 and 9 to balance the two limiting separations while keeping the last peak below 8 minutes. This may retain CRF 1.000 with a slightly larger minimum-resolution margin than injection 4.

Preserve the successful gradient through the first nine peaks, then test whether a hold at 50% organic elutes the final compound without a time penalty. This probes a lower-endpoint alternative while retaining the established maximum-scoring methods.

Test a slightly shallower gradient than injection 9 to strengthen its limiting 4–5 separation while checking that the 6–7 pair remains above 1.5. The predicted last-peak time is around 8.2 minutes, within the zero-penalty range demonstrated by injection 19.

Flatten the gradient relative to injection 10 to improve its limiting middle-pair resolution while preserving the stronger starting composition’s favorable separation of the other close pair. This tests whether a larger resolution margin can be achieved before the time penalty begins.

Preserve injection 9’s gradient slope and temperature while reducing the final organic fraction. The outlet gradient remains identical until 8.65 minutes, after all peaks previously eluted, so this alternative should retain CRF 1.000.

Slightly flatten injection 22’s gradient to improve the 4–5 separation while testing whether the 6–7 pair stays above 1.5. The final peak should remain near the demonstrated zero-time-penalty window, potentially preserving the maximum CRF at a lower endpoint.
Test a gradient slope between the maximum-scoring injections 20 and 23. Both neighboring slopes resolved all peaks without a time penalty, so this method is likely to preserve CRF 1.000.

Test a slightly steeper gradient than injection 22 to shorten retention while checking whether the limiting separation remains above 1.5. The campaign has already reached the maximum CRF of 1.000, so this final injection explores a faster alternative.
